name: PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bumi Resources Minerals: a gold ramp behind a konglo premium
frontmatter.summary: BRMS is a Bakrie-controlled gold miner whose Poboya pushback cut FY2026 output; the underground ramp and CIL expansion can lift volumes from FY2027. We anchor FY2026 to the nine-month actual, carry the full royalty and the funding cost the company pays, and find the shares already price a konglo premium and a gold price above the reviewed deck. We stay at HOLD after MSCI's November review moved the shares from the Standard to the Small Cap tier.
thesis: The Poboya underground mine and CIL expansion give BRMS a volume ramp from the pushback-depressed FY2026 base; we carry the company's timing but do not assume it beats schedule.
The FY2025 accounts show D&A far above the data pack; we restate cash flow and carry the gold royalty now in force.
At the deck's through-cycle gold price our life-of-asset DCF is below the market price; the shares already discount a successful ramp and a higher gold price.
The konglo lens, not the fundamental value, explains the next twelve months: the base case closes only part of the premium.
Risks are underground execution, the domestic gold oversupply discount, the royalty step-up, the funding path and the Bakrie group's capital-markets agenda.

catalysts.event: MSCI November 2026 rebalance takes effect after the close: BRMS leaves the Global Standard Indexes and joins the Global Small Cap Indexes
CIL plant capacity upgrade to the new throughput target
FY2026 results: first clean print of the post-pushback run-rate and the first test of the Q4 recovery
MSCI decision on Indonesia's Standalone status (konglo regime)
First high-grade underground ore from Poboya

blocks.text: **What changed (12 November 2026).** MSCI's November 2026 index review removed BRMS from the MSCI Global Standard Indexes and moved the shares into the Global Small Cap Indexes, in the same review that removed BRPT from the Standard tier, with the change taking effect after the close of 30 November 2026 [S16]. That is an event about who must sell, not about what the mine earns: it forces Standard-index trackers to sell at the rebalance, and it trims Indonesia's index weight by around 0.9 basis points on our reading of the press estimate [S17]. Nothing in our forecast depends on index membership — not the gold deck, not the ramp schedule, not the royalty or the funding path — so the rating stays **HOLD**.

**Why the target moved.** The twelve-month target is not a fixed fundamental anchor: the konglo overlay is price-linked, because the premium ratio is the share price divided by fundamental value, so the target itself moves with the price at the deck's compression share. Our published version target was set when the shares traded higher; the shares have since fallen, and most of that fall passes into the twelve-month target at the deck's compression share, which now stands at **Rp308** — the probability-weighted blend of the bear, base and bull regimes, with the base regime alone at Rp303 — against a last price of Rp310, an expected return of -0.5%. No operating forecast changed to produce that move. Two balance-sheet corrections did: the trading working-capital restatement removes a first-forecast-year cash release that was only ever a definition change, and the advances of US$136.2m at 30 September 2026 are now carried at carrying amount in the bridge as the asset that cash bought [S2][S3]. The target carries the lens's share of both, and a flow-driven de-rating would lower it mechanically in the same way. What changes with the November decision is the flow risk in the risks section, the bear-regime sensitivity in the valuation section and the monitoring list in the later section [S16][S17].

Our published view stands: PT Bumi Resources Minerals at **HOLD** with a twelve-month target of **Rp308**, against a last price of Rp310 — an expected return of -0.5%. The target is not the fundamental value: our life-of-asset DCF gives a fundamental twelve-month value of Rp218, while the shares trade at 1.6x times current fundamental value. The konglo lens only lets part of that premium decay within the year, which is why the target sits above the fundamental value but still close to today's price [S2][S3].

The variant view is straightforward. The market is paying for a successful underground ramp **and** a gold price well above the reviewed metals deck: the reverse DCF says today's price implies gold at about US$5,993/oz, or 1.4x the deck's through-cycle marker [S0]. We carry the ramp as the company plans it — the decline, the first ventilation shaft and the contractor are in place — but we do not assume it beats schedule, and the first forecast year is anchored to the nine-month actual rather than to the Board's earlier target. The base case therefore closes only 30.0% of the log premium, and the target return is negative [S9][S4][S6].

Three things move the value. First, the underground grade and timing: management targets high-grade ore above the reserve grade from the second half of 2027, and every quarter of delay pushes the volume ramp into a discounted year [S9][S2]. Second, the gold price: the deck's reviewed through-cycle marker is US$4,300/oz, sourced from the World Bank's price series, and the price implied by the shares is far above it [S11][S12]. Third, the royalty and cost base: the gold royalty rose in April 2025 and the domestic gold market is in oversupply, forcing discounted domestic sales or exports with a duty [S2][S4].

PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk is an Indonesian mineral explorer and producer listed on the IDX and controlled by the Bakrie group. Its core producing asset is PT Citra Palu Minerals (CPM), which holds a Contract of Work (Generation VI, 1997) over the Poboya gold project in Palu, Central Sulawesi; the construction and production permit was approved in 2017 with a production period running to 2050 [S4]. CPM is held almost entirely by BRMS, so almost all of the group's cash flow currently comes from a single gold mine [S2][S4].

The Poboya operation runs two carbon-in-leach plants. The second CIL plant has been processing at a steady rate, while the first is being upgraded to 2,000 tonnes per day, with completion targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026 [S4]. Below the open pit, CPM is developing an underground mine: the decline has advanced well below surface, the first ventilation shaft is complete, and management expects to start mining high-grade ore above the reserve grade in the middle of 2027 [S9]. The underground plan is a seventeen-year mine targeting about 2,800 koz of gold plus silver byproduct at an expected grade of 4.9 g/t [S2].

The reserve and resource base is the anchor. The 2024 JORC estimate puts CPM's mineral reserves at about 3,500 koz of gold at 3.2 g/t, with a larger mineral resource base [S2]. The 2025 resource statement totals 4,534 koz of contained gold, so roughly a quarter of the resource sits outside the reserve and is the tonnage a longer mine life or a higher extraction rate would draw on [S2]. That is a small reserve by Indonesian gold standards but a high grade by global open-pit standards, and it is the reason the underground project can carry a long life at a modest throughput [S2][S4].

The group also owns optionality outside Poboya. PT Gorontalo Minerals (majority-owned, with Antam holding the rest) holds a Contract of Work over a copper-gold concession in Gorontalo and is drilling, with more rigs planned next year [S2][S9]. PT Dairi Prima Mineral holds a zinc-lead asset, PT Linge Mineral Resources holds a gold IUP in Aceh whose AMDAL was approved in September 2025 but whose production permit was still pending, and PT Suma Heksa Sinergi holds a gold IUP in Banten [S2]. These are development assets; we value them at book inside the investment line rather than as producing cash flows [S0].

Revenue is almost entirely gold. FY2025 revenue was US$249.3m, with silver sales of only about US$7.0m of that total [S2][F7][F40]. The customer base is domestic — Hartadinata Abadi, Simba Jaya Utama and Swarnim Murni Mulia — and CPM also has a gold sales agreement with Pegadaian's gold retail network priced off the London Bullion Market PM bid, settled in rupiah at the Bank Indonesia middle rate [S2]. That domestic orientation supports margin stability but exposes the company to the periodic domestic oversupply discount that hit Q2-2026 sales [S4].

The strategy is to convert the open-pit cash flow into an underground mine and to keep exploring the copper and gold portfolio. The company has never paid a dividend and states that it retains cash for development [S2]. The group employed 954 people at the end of FY2025 [S2].

BRMS sits inside the Bakrie group's listed-vehicle complex, where the controlling family's capital-markets agenda — rights issues, placements, asset injections and index flows — has historically mattered as much as the mining P&L for the share price. The Poboya orebody is a high-grade epithermal system; underground mining is the standard route to extend its life once the oxide and transitional ore near surface is depleted. The domestic gold market is small relative to the mine's output, which is why Indonesian gold miners periodically sell at a discount at home or export with a duty.

Gold is the pricing variable that matters. The house metals deck carries the reviewed gold series at US$3,466/oz for FY2025A, US$4,494/oz for FY2026E and a through-cycle marker of US$4,300/oz from FY2027E. The series is not the annual report's forecast: its actuals and quarterly tape are the World Bank Pink Sheet (October 2026 edition), and its forward path is the World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook [S10][S11][S12]. The latest October 2026 Outlook puts gold at US$4,250/oz for 2027 and US$4,000/oz for 2028, so the deck's marker of US$4,300/oz is close to the newest 2027 public forecast, above current spot of US$3,987/oz and above the five-year actual average; it is not a pessimistic marker. The deck's path has the gold price easing from the 2026 average as the war premium and central-bank bid normalise; that mean reversion is the single largest driver of our valuation [S10][S11][S12].

Indonesia's gold sector is small and concentrated. The large producers are Freeport's Grasberg copper-gold complex, Antam's Pongkor and the newer copper-gold mines; BRMS is a mid-cap challenger with a single high-grade gold mine [S2]. The annual report's industry review describes a global gold market where mine supply is slow to respond and where Indonesian policy — royalties, permits and export rules — materially affects investment [S2]. BRMS is a price-taker: it sells domestically at a small discount to the London benchmark and has no pricing power [S2][S4].

Regulation is a first-order industry driver. The gold royalty rose to 16.0% in April 2025, and the company identifies that step-up as a direct pressure on FY2025 book margins [S2]. In May 2026 the government postponed a further planned royalty increase for gold and nickel while it reworked the formula, which leaves the current rate in place for our forecast [S8][S7]. The royalty is charged on the selling price, so it scales with the gold deck and is not a fixed cost [S2].

Domestic demand is the second regulatory channel. In Q2-2026 only part of BRMS's gold output was sold because the domestic market was oversupplied; management's mitigants are a discounted domestic sale or an export with a duty [S4]. That is a structural feature of the Indonesian gold market, not a one-off: a single mine's output can saturate local refining demand, so the realised price carries a discount and occasional inventory build [S4][S6]. The Q3-2026 recovery showed the discount easing as sales caught up, but the risk remains [S6].

On the cost curve, Poboya's reserve grade of 3.2 g/t and underground grade of 4.9 g/t place it in the lower half of the global gold cost curve on a cash-cost basis, even after the royalty step-up [S2]. The mine's cash cost ex-royalty can be read off the LK as cost of goods sold of US$109.1m less royalty of US$34.4m and non-cash D&A, on 71.9 koz sold in FY2025; at the deck's through-cycle gold price that leaves a healthy margin [S2][F2][F12][F15]. The moat is the orebody grade and the existing plant and permit, not scale or marketing [S4].

Five forces are mixed. Supplier power is moderate: the mining contractor Macmahon and the CIL plant suppliers are concentrated, but the company has demonstrated it can commission capacity [S4][S9]. Buyer power is high because the domestic gold market is small and alternative buyers are refiners or exporters with a duty [S4]. New entrants are constrained by permitting and the capital cost of a new mine, but the underground project itself shows how quickly capacity can be added inside an existing permit [S2]. Substitutes are minimal for gold as an investment metal. Rivalry among Indonesian gold producers is modest but the global gold price is the binding constraint [S2].

The external influences we monitor are the gold price, the rupiah, the royalty formula and the domestic gold balance. The deck's gold path and the macro desk's USD/IDR path are the two market inputs; the royalty and export rules are policy inputs [S2][S8]. A stronger rupiah lowers the IDR value of USD gold revenue and of the USD-reported dividend capacity, while a weaker rupiah helps [S0].

BRMS's reported history is a ramp story. Revenue rose from US$46.6m in FY2023 to US$249.4m in FY2025, as gold sales volume reached 71.9 koz and the average gold price rose to US$3,371/oz from US$2,442/oz [S2]. Net profit to parent reached US$50.0m, a 20.1% margin, and ROE was 4.1% on a large equity base that still carries the historical investment in the group's other projects [S2][S0]. The FY2025 EBITDA margin was 39.8% on our restated D&A [S2].

The first nine months of 2026 are weaker. Revenue was US$167.6m and net profit US$23.9m, down from the prior-year period, because the River Reef pushback cut ore tonnes and grade through the first half [S6][S5]. Q3-2026 was the turning point: sales recovered to 16.7 koz at an average price of US$4,128/oz and the processed grade rose to 1.9 g/t as the pushback was completed in July [S6][S9]. We model FY2026E sales of 55 koz — the actual nine-month run-rate plus a fourth quarter at the Q3 pace, not an unquantified inventory sell-down — and not the Board's earlier 80 koz target, which the nine-month print has already refuted [S2][S4][S6].

**The FY2026E bridge from the nine-month actual.** We build the year from the actual rather than from a margin. Sales are 55 koz — the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the Q3 pace [S6][S4]. Costs are the nine-month actuals at the unit-cost line: nine-month COGS of US$75.0m on nine-month sales of US$167.6m, which after the royalty and D&A leaves a unit cash cost well above the FY2025 full-year rate, because the pushback depressed grade and throughput. We therefore set the FY2026E unit cash cost from that print and revert to the FY2025 rate from FY2027E as grade recovers (590 and 500 per ounce against 503 and 426). Interest is the second correction: the nine-month accounts already carry US$20.4m of interest and finance charges, an annualised charge well above a rate on the FY2025 closing balance, so the FY2026E interest base is calibrated to it at 14.3% [S3]. The result is FY2026E parent profit of US$49.5m against the nine-month actual of US$23.9m, so the fourth quarter carries more profit than the whole nine months [S3][S6]. That weighting is deliberate and sourced rather than a Q3 run-rate multiplied out: the pushback cut first-half grade and throughput, so the nine-month margin is depressed and not representative, while the fourth quarter sells at the Q3 pace with the recovered grade [S6][S4][S5]. Operating expenses are the one line where we do not extrapolate the nine-month print: nine-month operating expenses were US$40.5m on revenue of US$167.6m, a ratio lifted by the pushback-depressed revenue base, so the forecast holds the FY2025 full-year ratio of 18.9% and does not revert it upward; carrying the nine-month ratio instead would lower FY2026E EBITDA and the DCF by an amount too small to change the rating or the rounded target [S3][S2].

**What Yahoo gets wrong, and what we restate.** The data pack's D&A is US$1.1m — only the depreciation charged to operating expenses. LK note eleven reports depreciation charged to profit or loss of US$6.2m (cost of revenue plus opex), and note twelve adds mining-property amortisation of US$2.9m; total D&A is therefore the sum of the two notes, roughly eight times the pack's line [S2]. We carry that total charge in the forecast at US$126.1 per ounce; in the restated history the engine adds the note eleven depreciation to EBIT to rebuild EBITDA at US$99.3m, while the note twelve amortisation sits inside cost of revenue as the LK reports it [S2]. Capex, by contrast, is right in the pack: the FY2025 US$69.2m equals the cash-flow statement's fixed-asset purchases, mining-property additions and exploration-and-evaluation payments added together [S2]. Dividends are zero and have always been zero [S2]. The share count is 141,784,040,338 shares [S2]. Interest expense of US$18.1m and interest income of US$0.6m match the LK [S2].

The cash-cost build is the one we use. FY2025 COGS of US$109.1m contains royalty of US$34.4m, depreciation of US$6.2m and mining-property amortisation of US$2.9m; the residual is the cash cost ex-royalty that the model carries per ounce, with mining cost of US$36.2m and the balance processing, maintenance, utilities and labour [S2]. We hold those unit costs flat in nominal dollars and let them escalate after the explicit forecast, so the model does not silently assume a margin expansion [S2]. The silver credit is no longer frozen at the FY2025 level: it is scaled with the gold-ounce plan at the plan's silver-to-gold ratio and priced off the reviewed silver series, so it grows from about US$8.3m to US$23.0m as the ramp arrives rather than being escalated at a constant rate [S2][S10].

Working capital needs a restatement too. The data pack's non-cash working capital line included advances to suppliers and contractors and prepaid taxes, which are project and period items rather than revenue-scaled operating working capital [S2]. We restate the history to the accounts' own trade working capital — trade receivables plus inventories less trade payables, US$9.9m at FY2025 and US$6.0m at FY2024 — and model operating working capital at 4.0% of revenue. That restatement is what removes the apparent first-year cash release: with the pack's broader line still in history, the first forecast year booked a release equal to the whole non-operating balance purely from the definition change, and no such cash arrives. The FY2026E change in working capital is now US$0.0m [S2]. The non-operating balances are not dropped: the advances of US$136.2m at 30 September 2026 are carried at carrying amount in the bridge in the valuation section [S3]. Any Q2-2026 ore release is upside, since the ore balance is not disclosed [S4].

The balance sheet has shifted from a net-cash position to a leveraged development balance sheet. At the September 2026 date, cash was lower than the year-end figure and debt had risen to fund the underground and plant, so net debt is materially above the FY2025 figure of US$149.3m [S3]. The company arranged a US$625m syndicated facility in late 2025, of which US$425m is earmarked for the Poboya underground and CIL upgrade and the rest for exploration in Gorontalo, Aceh and Banten [S2]. At the September 2026 date US$294.3m of bank loans was outstanding under the syndicated facility, after US$128.0m of drawdowns and US$13.7m of repayments in the nine months [S3]. We carry the project capex in capex_other through FY2028E and assume the related drawdowns [S2].

Earnings quality is good on the cash test. Operating cash flow exceeded net profit in FY2025, so the accruals ratio is negative; the divergence flags are not present — receivables and inventory are small relative to revenue, and the margin expansion is explained by the gold price and the higher grade, not by capitalised costs [S0][S2]. The one governance-adjacent flow is the US$21.7m due from related parties, a modest share of revenue but a reminder of the group's related-party footprint [S2]. There is no special-monitoring-board status, no notation flag and no auditor change: RSM Indonesia signed an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 accounts [S2].

We value BRMS on a life-of-asset DCF at through-cycle gold, which is the house method for commodity producers and the right one here: the mine has a finite reserve, the gold price is the dominant variable, and current-year multiples would capitalise a cycle position rather than the asset [S2]. The DCF discounts explicit annual free cash flow to the end of the reserve, with no terminal value, so a long mine life is worth what it can actually produce [S2].

The cost of capital is built from the house parameters. The risk-free rate is 5.0%, the mature-market equity risk premium 4.2% and the Indonesia country risk premium 2.5%; the unlevered beta is 1.0, levered to 1.10 at the company's debt-to-equity, giving a cost of equity of 12.8%. The pre-tax cost of debt in the generic build is 7.0%, the USD risk-free rate plus the house corporate spread, but BRMS actually pays about twelve percent on its drawn facilities [S2][S3]. The two numbers cannot both stand, so we add a company financing premium of 0.5% to the cost of equity, set so that its contribution to the WACC equals the after-tax debt-cost gap at the company's debt weight; that lifts the WACC to 12.0% and lowers the DCF by about three percent versus the generic build [S2][S3].

The primary DCF gives a value of Rp213 per share. We do not blend a P/BV cross-check: BRMS's book equity is distorted by a negative minority-interest deficit and a return on equity of only 4.1%, so accounting book is not a value anchor. The EV/EBITDA cross-check is also unavailable: none of the five registered peers in the industry comps (AMMN, ARCI, EMAS, PSAB, SQMI) carries a usable EV/EBITDA method value, and the peer medians that exist rest on data-pack trailing quotes rather than a house-computed peer set. The fundamental value is the life-of-asset DCF; with the cross-check removed the rating rests on the DCF and the konglo lens, and the resulting rating is HOLD on a target of Rp308. The table shows the DCF with its bridge [S0][S2][S3].

The bridge is explicit. Enterprise value from the DCF is US$1,490.9m; net debt is deducted — total borrowings at 30 September 2026, of which the US$294.3m of outstanding syndicated bank loans is the bulk, less US$30.6m of cash, materially above the audited FY2025 net debt of US$149.3m [S3]. Two non-operating items sit beside it. First, the advances of US$136.2m at the balance-sheet date are added at carrying amount: they are cash already paid for plant and infrastructure development at GM and for supplier capital goods, which the US$425m Poboya facility programme does not fund, so the same cash is not spent twice, and the carrying amount is the audited number rather than a mark we have made [S3][S2]. Second, the working-capital definition: the history is restated to trade working capital of US$9.9m, which turns the first forecast year's apparent release into a change of US$0.0m. The release and the advance are the same balance-sheet money — the release was only ever a definition change prorated to the part-year stub of the first forecast year, and the paid advance is the asset it left behind — so the two must not be added as if each were new value [S2][S3]. Because the removed release's present value depends on the engine's stub discount and is not separately archived, we state the two effects rather than a net per-share figure: the advance is carried at its audited carrying amount, and the restatement removes a release that no longer appears, leaving the FY2026E change in working capital at US$0.0m [S2][S3]. Associates and joint ventures are added at book of US$332.6m; the bulk is the non-controlling interest in PT Dairi Prima Mineral, a pre-production zinc-lead JV, alongside Gorontalo, Linge and Suma Heksa [S3][S2]. Book is used here not as a value anchor but as the last audited carrying amount of assets with no production or reserve we can discount; the carrying-value test is that Dairi has not been impaired and the group's share of JV losses is immaterial, so book is an audited number rather than a mark we have made. The non-controlling-interest line is a deficit of US$210.1m [S3]. The engine subtracts NCI, which mechanically adds that deficit to the equity value; a deficit is accumulated losses, not an asset, so we carry a bridge charge of the same size to remove it. The minority is handled once: the model charges the minorities' share of profit in the profit and loss account, and the bridge removes only the balance-sheet deficit that the engine's arithmetic would otherwise add to equity, so the two are not double-counted. The per-share effect is in the valuation table [S3].

The bull case is a mine-plan case, not a resource case. It applies the volume and gold shocks shown in the table to the 4.9 g/t underground grade, which is worth Rp301 a share against Rp241 in the base [S2][S4]. The resource outside the 3,500 koz reserve (4,534 koz in total) is not sized: it has no converted reserve, no mine plan and no feasibility study, so its only defensible value is an option value we cannot source, and we price it at zero rather than at a multiple of ounces. The same test applies to Gorontalo, Dairi and Linge — exploration-stage or pre-production, carried at book, named as optionality but not valued in the bull — which is why the bull is a schedule-and-price case rather than a sum-of-assets case [S2][S3][S9].

The sensitivity table shows what matters: a gold move of the size shown is worth several hundred rupiah per share, and the two-year ramp delay is worth a similar amount — which is why the bear case now carries a volume shock sized to that delay rather than a pure price haircut. The royalty rate and the cash-cost assumptions are second-order by comparison, which is why we spend our time on the volume ramp and the gold deck rather than on cost micro-tuning [S2][S9].

What does today's price imply? The reverse DCF says the shares discount a gold price of about US$5,993/oz, or 1.4x the reviewed through-cycle marker of US$4,300/oz, **and** the full underground ramp [S0][S11][S12]. That is the variant view in one number: the market is not paying for Poboya as it is; it is paying for Poboya plus a much better gold price.

**The konglo lens.** BRMS is a Bakrie-group vehicle, so the twelve-month price is set at the margin by the concentrated-ownership regime, not only by fundamental value [S2][S15]. The lens measures the price against the probability-weighted fundamental value across our scenarios — Rp193 a share today, below the Rp213 base-case DCF because the bear case is weighted in — and keeps part of that premium — 1.6x times our fundamental value — over three regime scenarios: the base case closes 30.0% of the log gap in twelve months, the bear case closes 70.0% and the bull regime lets the premium re-expand [S0]. That produces a probability-weighted blend of Rp308 across the three regimes — bear Rp251, base Rp303 and bull Rp376 at the weights in the table — against a fundamental twelve-month value of Rp218 [S0]. So the headline target is the blend, not the base-regime row: 30.0% of the log premium applied to the 1.6x gap gives the Rp303 base regime, and the blend adds the bear and bull legs at their probabilities. The float arithmetic is the reason the base, not the bear, is the most likely path: the free float is 51.2% against the exchange's new minimum of 15.0%, which rose from the earlier level, so there is no free-float step due inside the window; the audited shareholding table shows 47.0% in public hands at the last year-end as a cross-check; the name is not on the high-shareholding-concentration list; and the house konglo registry records no index deletion or enforcement action for it [S0][S2][S14][S18]. The registry snapshot predates the 12 November decision, so we say plainly that its empty index-deletion field is stale as of that date. The November review moves the shares out of the Standard tier into Small Cap rather than out of the MSCI universe, so on the registry's definition it is not a deletion; but a reader is entitled to test the other reading, and the sensitivity is in the table: if the demotion is treated as a regime flag, the lens applies the bear-regime compression of 70.0% and the twelve-month target is Rp251, below today's price. We carry that as a sensitivity rather than as a silent target cut, because the event changes who must sell, not what the mine earns [S16][S17][S18]. With no regime flag, the lens applies the deck's no-flag default closing share of 30.0% in the base regime; the March 2027 and March 2028 free-float steps that dominate narrow-float konglo names do not apply here. The dated regime catalyst inside the twelve-month window is the MSCI decision on Indonesia's Standalone status by 30 June 2027: a Standalone outcome would push BRMS toward the bear regime and a maintained Emerging-market status leaves the base case [S13]. The name-specific catalysts are operational — CIL commissioning, the second ventilation shaft and first underground ore [S4][S9].

Konglo stocks trade on float and flows: a small free float means index inclusion or deletion, a group rights issue or a retail momentum wave can move the price far from what the mine is worth. The house lens does not bend the mine's cash flows to explain the price; it takes the fundamental value as given and asks how much of the current premium is likely to survive the year. That is why the target can sit above the fundamental value even when the shares are expensive.
The downside risks, with our likelihood and impact:

items: **Underground execution (medium likelihood, high impact).** The ramp to high-grade ore is the value driver; a delay of a year or a grade shortfall would push the volume ramp into later, more heavily discounted years [S9][S2].
**Gold price (medium likelihood, high impact).** A return to the deck's lower through-cycle path, or a policy-driven gold sell-off, cuts revenue directly; the bear gold shock is in the table [S2].

**Royalty and tax (high likelihood, medium impact).** The gold royalty of 16.0% is already in force; a further increase, or a change in the base on which it is charged, would take a visible slice of revenue [S2][S8].
**Domestic gold oversupply and export duty (medium likelihood, medium impact).** A repeat of the Q2-2026 discount, or a higher export duty, lowers realised prices and can build inventory [S4].
**FX (low likelihood, medium impact).** A stronger rupiah lowers the IDR value of USD gold revenue and the reported dividend capacity [S0].

**Governance and the konglo premium (high likelihood, high impact).** The stock's premium to fundamental value is a regime variable; a market-wide de-rating of concentrated-ownership names, or a group corporate action, can compress it faster than the mine's cash flow can grow [S2].

**Index membership and passive flows (high likelihood, low fundamental impact, medium price impact).** The November 2026 review takes BRMS out of the MSCI Global Standard Indexes and into the Global Small Cap Indexes, so Standard-tracker funds must sell into the 30 November 2026 rebalance. The only name-level flow estimate in the pack is a combined figure of Rp1,200bn for BRPT and BRMS together, which we quote as an upper bound because the source does not split it by name, alongside the estimate that Indonesia's index weight falls by about 0.9 basis points [S16][S17]. The selling is mechanical and dated, not a view on the mine; with a 51.2% free float the exit is absorbable, but a Small Cap seat is the thinner tier and the residual index bid would go if Indonesia were moved to MSCI Standalone at the June 2027 decision [S13]. Because the registry snapshot predates the decision, the bear-regime line in the valuation is the test of the other reading [S16].
**Liquidity and leverage (medium likelihood, medium impact).** Net debt has risen with the project; a slower ramp with a US$625m facility to service is a real constraint [S3][S2].

**Funding and dilution (medium likelihood, high impact).** The facility is the funding source, not the equity market: US$294.3m was outstanding at September 2026 against a US$625m facility, so the undrawn balance is the difference between those two facts and the base forecast's project capex fits inside it [S3][S2]. In the bear — a gold shock and a two-year ramp delay — FY2027E free cash flow is negative, but the cumulative shortfall we see is smaller than that undrawn balance, which is why the bear carries a higher cost of capital rather than a dilution shock. If the facility were exhausted, the Bakrie group's rights-issue history makes a discounted equity raise the likely path; the method card's serial-rights-issue flag is the reason we name it as the tail rather than model a share count we cannot size from a disclosed source [S3][S2].

**Permitting (medium likelihood, medium impact).** Linge's production permit and Gorontalo's copper work are optionality, not base-case cash flow; a permit delay does not hurt the base but removes the upside [S2].

blocks.text: The business scenarios are mirrored on the drivers that have a two-sided source. The bear case cuts gold and lifts the cost of capital for the funding spread. Its volume shock is larger than the gold shock, because it also carries the two-year ramp delay that removes the FY2028E first full underground year: that delay has no mirrored upside, because the bull cannot mine earlier than the company's own schedule (the decline, first shaft and contractor are already in place), so the volume shock is the one deliberately asymmetric driver and it is disclosed as such. The bear also cuts realisation a further notch for the oversupply/export-duty channel, a downside wedge with no symmetric source [S2][S4][S9]. It values the shares at Rp89; the base is Rp241 and the bull, on the shocks shown in the table, is Rp301 at a higher volume on the 4.9 g/t underground grade. The probabilities are in the table; the base case is above the house minimum because the mine plan is sourced and the facility covers the base funding path [S2][S3][S4]. The realisation shock is not invented: in Q2-2026 only 70.0% of output was sold and the realised price fell from US$4,512/oz in Q1 to US$4,138/oz in Q2, while the export alternative carries a duty [S4]. The base case holds the FY2025 realised-to-benchmark ratio, so the bear is a downside wedge, not the base path [S2][S4].

The regime scenarios are separate and are the ones that set the twelve-month target. In the bear regime, 70.0% of the log premium closes and the target is Rp251; in the base regime, 30.0% closes and the target is Rp303; in the bull regime the premium re-expands and the target is Rp376 [S0]. The dated regime catalyst is the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 June 2027 [S13]; the free-float steps that dominate other konglo names do not apply here because BRMS is already compliant with the 15.0% minimum, and the quarterly HSC list is a monitoring item rather than a scheduled event [S14][S18]. The November 2026 demotion from the Standard to the Small Cap tier is the first index-flow event to land on this name. We do not put it in the DCF's cash flows, because it changes the buyer base rather than the mine, and we do not read it as evidence that the Standalone consultation resolves against Indonesia [S16][S17][S13]. We do put it where it belongs: the combined outflow estimate is quoted above, and the bear-regime target is one table away, so a reader can see what the flow event costs if it is read as a regime flag rather than as a dated sale [S16][S17].

The signposts that would change our view are: the first underground ore grade printed above the reserve grade; CIL commissioning on time; the domestic gold discount narrowing for two consecutive quarters; the gold deck's through-cycle marker moving; and the konglo premium narrowing without a fundamental improvement, which would turn a HOLD into a more attractive entry.

BRMS is controlled by the Bakrie family. The President Commissioner is Adika Nuraga Bakrie, two Bakrie family members sit on the Board of Directors, and the group's listed holding company, PT Bumi Resources, is one of the two largest shareholders alongside Emirates Tarian Global Ventures [S2][S15]. The free float is 51.2%, against the exchange minimum of 15.0% that replaced the earlier threshold; the audited shareholding table shows 47.0% in public hands at the last year-end as a cross-check, and the company is **not** on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list [S0][S2][S14][S18]; there are no index deletions or OJK enforcement actions against it in the konglo registry — the November 2026 loss of the Standard seat is a downgrade within the MSCI universe, since the shares are retained in the Small Cap tier, not a deletion from it [S16]. That is a better governance starting point than many konglo names, but the group relationship still matters for related-party flows and for the stock's flow-driven premium [S2].

The overlay is why the target sits above the fundamental value rather than at it. The shares trade at 1.6x times our fundamental value; in the base regime 30.0% of the log premium closes over twelve months, producing a base-regime target of Rp303, and the probability-weighted blend across the bear, base and bull regimes is Rp308 against a fundamental twelve-month value of Rp218 [S2][S0]. With a 51.2% free float against the exchange minimum of 15.0%, there is no free-float deadline for this name and no HSC flag to force a faster close; the one index event on the calendar is the 30 November 2026 rebalance that moves the shares to the Small Cap tier, which we treat as a dated passive outflow rather than a regime flag, so the 30.0% base remains the deck's no-flag default [S0][S2][S14][S16][S18]. If that reading is wrong and the demotion is a regime flag, the bear-regime target of Rp251 is the value we would publish [S16][S17]. The dated regime catalyst is the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 June 2027 [S13]. The target is therefore a regime call, not a fundamental re-rating: it asks only for a partial normalisation of a premium that the controlling group and flow-driven demand have sustained [S2].

Related-party exposure is modest in absolute terms but present. The company had US$21.7m due from related parties at the end of FY2025, alongside a small related-party payable, and it discloses the usual affiliate relationships on the board [S2]. There is no disclosed pledge of the controlling shareholder's BRMS shares; the security for the bank facilities is CPM's fixed assets and the project's plant, not the listed shares [S2]. The auditor is RSM Indonesia, which issued an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 consolidated accounts; the audit committee is chaired by an independent commissioner [S2].

The dividend record is empty: the company has never paid a dividend and states that it will retain cash for development and for its creditors [S2]. That is consistent with the investment phase, but it means the market's anchor is not dividend capacity — it is the asset value and the konglo premium [S2].

ESG exposure is typical for Indonesian gold mining. The company holds AMDAL approvals for its projects and carries a mine-rehabilitation provision; the Poboya operation uses a CIL process, so cyanide handling, tailings management and water use are the material environmental issues [S2]. The underground mine reduces surface disturbance relative to a larger open pit, but it also adds ventilation and ground-control risks [S9]. Socially, the Palu operation depends on community acceptance and local employment; the annual report describes community-development spending but does not quantify it in a way we can model [S2].

The dated catalysts are the MSCI rebalance after the close of 30 November 2026, when the shares leave the Global Standard Indexes for the Small Cap tier, the CIL upgrade in the fourth quarter of 2026, the second ventilation shaft in the first half of 2027, first high-grade underground ore in the second half of 2027 and the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 June 2027 [S16][S4][S9][S13]. The FY2026 results in early 2027 will be the first clean print of the post-pushback run-rate and the first test of whether the fourth-quarter recovery held [S6]. There is no free-float compliance step for BRMS: it is already above the exchange's minimum and is not on the HSC list [S0][S14].

Between updates we watch a short list of KPIs. Gold sales volume in ounces and the processed grade in grams per tonne are the two operating numbers that tell us whether the ramp is real; the plant throughput and the CIL commissioning date are the leading indicators [S4][S9]. The realised gold price against the deck's benchmark tells us whether the domestic discount is widening or narrowing [S6]. The royalty and tax payments in the cash-flow statement tell us whether the current royalty rate is being applied as expected [S2]. Net debt and the facility drawdown tell us whether the project is funded without a rights issue [S3]. And the konglo regime — free float, HSC status, index decisions and group corporate actions — tells us how much of the premium the market is likely to keep [S2]. The first reading on the index-flow question is the traded volume and foreign net flow around the 30 November 2026 rebalance: if the Standard exit is absorbed without a widening discount to the Small Cap index, the flow risk in the risks section is priced and the premium path stands [S16][S17]. The house konglo registry still shows no index deletion as of its 27 October 2026 snapshot; that entry is stale after the 12 November review and is flagged for correction, so until it is updated we carry the event through the bear-regime sensitivity rather than through the no-flag default [S16][S17].

bear.narrative: The underground ramp slips beyond 2027 and the open pit stays low-grade after the pushback, so the volume path is cut 20 percent rather than the 10 percent the pure price case would give; gold mean-reverts below the deck's through-cycle mark, the domestic oversupply discount reopens (only 70% of Q2-2026 output sold, S4 p.9) and the funding spread rises as the project draws against the facility. The volume shock is the delay risk the report ranks beside the gold price: a two-year slip in first high-grade underground ore (targeted 2H2027, S9) removes the FY2028E first-full-underground year. Volume is cut 20 percent, the gold price 20 percent lower, realisation a further 5 percent lower and the cost of capital 150bp higher, cutting NAV. The facility headroom is the reason a rights issue is not the base-case funding path; if the facility were exhausted, the Bakrie group's rights-issue history makes dilution the likely route.

bull.narrative: The underground reaches the 4.9 g/t ore on schedule, CIL-1 expands to 2,000 tpd and the gold price holds above the deck's through-cycle mark. The 17-year underground plan extracts 2.8 Moz at 4.9 g/t against a 4.5 Moz total resource and a 3.5 Moz reserve at 3.2 g/t (F34/F35/F54), so the grade and tonnage support a 10% volume uplift without drawing on the resource outside the reserve. The resource outside the 3,500 koz reserve is not sized here: it has no converted reserve, no mine plan and no feasibility study, so it is worth its option value, not a discounted cash flow, and we price it at zero rather than at a multiple we cannot source. The Gorontalo copper-gold and Dairi zinc assets are carried at book in the associates line and are exploration-stage or pre-production, so they are optionality that the bull narrative names rather than values. Gold is 20% higher.

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 54,600 oz: 9M2026 actual gold sales were 37,839 oz (Q1 14,790 F29 + Q2 6,301 F30 + Q3 16,748 F26); the River Reef pushback that cut Q4-2025 to Q2-2026 output was completed in July 2026 (S9) and Q3 sales ran at a 67 koz annual rate, so the fourth quarter is set at the Q3 run-rate rather than on an unquantified inventory sell-down. The Q2 print (only 70% of output sold, S4 p.9) leaves a catch-up possibility, but the company does not disclose the unsold-ounce balance, so the most likely anchor is the latest actual quarter; any Q2 stockpile release is upside, not base. The Board's 80,000 oz 2026 target (F33) was set before the two-quarter pushback and is not reachable from a 37.8 koz nine-month print; we do not model a target the actuals refute. FY2027E 80,000 oz: underground ore at 4.9 g/t starts mid/late 2027 (F34; S9) while the open pit runs a full year and CIL-1 reaches 2,000 tpd (F36). FY2028E 140,000 oz is the first full underground year, and FY2029E-FY2030E 165,000 oz is the steady state implied by the company's 2.8 Moz over a 17-year underground life (F35); 165 koz also sits inside the 6,000 tpd plant at the reserve grade. No volume decline is assumed beyond the sourced FY2026 pushback year.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the last actual: FY2025A average gold selling price was US$3,371/oz (F5) against the metals deck's FY2025A gold average of US$3,466.09/oz, a ratio of 0.9726. The ratio is held flat across the forecast, NOT fitted to the FY2026E deck spike (4,493.75) — fitting to a peak would carry a trough realised price into the long run. The ~2.7% discount is consistent with domestic refining and the Pegadaian/LBMA-PM sales agreement (S2 p.123); Q3-2026 realised US$4,128/oz against the deck's Q3-2026 average is the same order of discount (F27).

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 because this is an underground/open-pit gold ore model priced per ounce, not a coal-style bcm stripping model; cost_per_bcm therefore carries the mining cash cost per ounce directly (S2 p.314 cost-of-sales note). The company does disclose a stripping ratio for the open pit (S4 p.12), but ore tonnes and grade, not bcm, drive gold output.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 mining cash cost was US$36.188m (F14) on 71,886 oz sold = US$503.4/oz. For FY2026E we use the nine-month actual unit cost: 9M2026 COGS of US$75.035m (F58, S3 p.6) less royalty at 16% of 9M sales (US$26.8m) less 9M D&A of about US$7m leaves US$41.2m of cash cost on 37,839 oz sold = US$1,090/oz, split between mining and processing in the FY2025 proportion (54.2% / 45.8%), i.e. US$590/oz mining. FY2027E reverts to the FY2025 unit rate as the pushback-depressed grade and throughput recover. Held flat in nominal USD and escalated at the engine's USD long-run rate thereafter. The mining cost includes the Macmahon contract and owner mining.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Cash cost excluding royalty and D&A was US$66.797m in FY2025 (COGS US$109.130m F15 less royalty US$34.368m F12 less depreciation US$6.164m F9 less amortisation US$2.901m F10); after the US$36.188m mining cost (F14) the remaining processing, maintenance, utilities and labour cost is US$30.609m = US$425.8/oz. FY2026E carries US$500/oz, the processing share of the 9M2026 actual unit cost of US$1,090/oz (F58, S3 p.6); FY2027E reverts to the FY2025 rate. Held flat in nominal USD, escalated after FY2030E.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: PP 19/2025 raised the gold royalty from 10% to 16% effective April 2025 (F41, S2 p.40; S7), so a full forward year carries 16%. FY2025's 13.8% effective take (F12/F7) is a transition blend of the 10% rate through March and 16% from April; the FY2024 take was 9.9% (F13/F6). Using the rate now in force is the most-likely forward assumption and the calibration gap it creates versus FY2025 is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Other revenue (silver byproduct)
assumptions.basis: Silver is priced off the reviewed metals deck and scaled with the gold-ounce plan rather than frozen at the FY2025 level. FY2025 revenue split: gold sales US$242.3m and silver sales US$7.04m (F40); the company's underground plan carries about 6 Moz of silver alongside 2.8 Moz of gold (F35), a ratio of 2.14 silver ounces per gold ounce. We apply that ratio to the volume plan and price it at the reviewed silver series (FY2026E US$71.25/oz, FY2027E onward US$65.00/oz, deck metals.silver; the FY2025A deck average was US$40.12/oz), so the credit grows with the ramp and with the silver deck rather than being escalated at 2% in perpetuity. The FY2025 implied silver output of about 175 koz sits inside the 6 Moz plan.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Silver is a byproduct: the mining and processing cost is already charged against gold in other_cost_unit, so the silver credit carries no incremental cash cost. Using 1.0 avoids double-counting the ore cost.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A per the LK notes: depreciation charged to profit or loss US$6.164m (F9) plus mining-property amortisation US$2.901m (F10) = US$9.064m on 71,886 oz = US$126.1/oz. The data pack's US$1.098m captured only the opex depreciation line; it is restated here. Held at US$126.1/oz across the forecast as a unit-of-production charge; the underground capex adds depreciable assets, so this is not a conservative-low charge.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 reported capex of US$69.2m was dominated by the underground-mine and CIL-1 expansion (mining-property additions US$29.3m and fixed-asset purchases US$38.2m, S2 p.242), not by sustaining spend. We carry sustaining capex at US$130/oz, close to the D&A rate (F9/F10) — the replacement rate for an ageing plant — and put the US$425m underground/plant project in capex_other (F38). This avoids charging the one-off project as perpetual sustaining capex.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: The US$425m CPM facility is earmarked for completion of the Poboya underground mine and the CIL-1 capacity upgrade to 2,000 tpd (F38, S2 p.25); we spread it FY2026E US$150m, FY2027E US$200m, FY2028E US$75m and nothing after, matching the 2027 start-up and 2028 first full year. The separate US$200m exploration tranche is expensed/capitalised as E&E and is not in this line. The US$136.2m of advances at 30 September 2026 (F61, S3 note 9) are payments already made — US$90.4m of plant and infrastructure development at GM and US$45.1m of supplier advances for capital goods — not part of this future facility programme: they are carried at face in the valuation bridge, so the Poboya spend is charged once and the same cash is not spent twice.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The data pack's non-cash working capital (US$156.2m) includes US$138.1m of advances, US$35.6m of prepaid taxes and other project/period items (S2 p.110), none of which is revenue-scaled operating working capital. The history is therefore restated to the accounts' own trade working capital — trade receivables plus inventories less trade payables: US$9.87m at FY2025 (F62) and US$5.95m at FY2024 (F63) — which is 4.0% of FY2025 revenue, the ratio we carry. The non-operating balances are not dropped: the advances are carried in the valuation bridge (F61) and prepaid taxes are a tax-timing asset already reflected in the effective tax rate. Restating the definition is what removes the apparent FY2026E cash release: with the pack's line still in history the engine booked a US$146.3m "release" in FY2026E purely from moving to a 4% ratio, and that release is not a cash flow. The Q2-2026 inventory build is real (S4 p.9) but the ore balance is not disclosed, so the last audited ratio is the only sourced anchor. Disclosed in sections 3 and 4.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 tax expense US$16.180m on pre-tax profit US$66.267m = 24.4% (S2 p.239), held flat; FY2024 was 26.1%. This is the rate the audited accounts show, not a statutory 22% assumption.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The nine-month accounts already carry US$20.358m of interest and finance charges (F57, S3 p.6), an annualised US$27.1m, against opening FY2026 debt of US$189.8m = 14.3%. That is the rate the company actually pays on the drawn US$625m syndicated facility, above both the FY2025 blended rate (US$18.118m F21 on about US$147m average debt) and the engine's three-year default. We use 14.3% on opening debt so FY2026E interest reconciles to the 9M2026 actual.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income US$0.593m (F22) on opening cash US$11.8m is 5.0%; held at 5%.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Debt rose from US$189.8m at FY2025 to US$307.0m at Q3-2026 (F42, S3), a US$117m draw; we assume a further US$80m in FY2027E and US$30m in FY2028E as the remaining CPM project facility is drawn, then zero. The US$625m facility is the source (F37); financing does not enter FCFF, so this only sets the interest and balance-sheet path.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The company has never paid a dividend and says it will retain cash for mine development (S2 p.127: "Perseroan belum melakukan pembagian dividen kepada pemegang saham"). Payout is zero across the forecast; the dividend-capacity cross-check is therefore theoretical.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating expenses US$47.042m (F17) on revenue US$249.354m (F7) = 18.9%, held flat. The FY2023-FY2025 average (20.4%) overstates the current scale because FY2024 revenue was still ramping; the last actual is the right anchor. The nine-month 2026 print is 24.2% (US$40.538m opex on US$167.58m revenue, F65/F31, S3 p.6) but that ratio sits on a revenue base depressed by the River Reef pushback, so we do not extrapolate it into the first forecast year; holding the full-year FY2025 ratio rather than the nine-month ratio is the difference the FY2026E bridge discloses, and it is under US$8m of EBITDA.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities were 1.6% of net profit on the FY2023-FY2025 average (S0 data pack); the main minority is the 3.03% of CPM not owned. Held at 1.6%.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The primary method is a life-of-asset DCF with no terminal value, so this parameter is inert; it is set at the house USD long-run inflation rate for completeness (S0 macro deck).

challenges.challenge: The summary says the twelve-month target stays at Rp301, but published v1 was HOLD/Rp323 with TR -5.0 percent and the model now prints Rp301/-3.1 percent. Nothing in the forecast changed: the fall is the overlay price link (premium_ratio = price / v_fundamental, so roughly 70 percent of the share-price fall from about Rp340 to Rp310 passes into the base-regime target). The live qc_justification for konglo.overlay in fund record still reads the target of 323. Required: state that the target moved 323 to 301 because the price did, disclose that the overlay is price-linked so a flow-driven de-rating lowers the target mechanically, and refresh the stale justification.
challenges.answer: Summary now states the target is price-linked: premium_ratio = price / v_fundamental, so most of the share-price fall passes into the base-regime target; the move from the published target is explained as overlay linkage, not a forecast change, and the stale qc_justification is rewritten. [S2][S3]

challenges.challenge: The event that triggered this update has exactly zero weight in the valuation: the summary says what changes is the flow risk in the risks and scenarios section, but the scenarios and overlay parameters are unchanged (fund record not touched) and section 5 says we leave it outside the compression deck. The no-flag default the target rests on comes from a registry dated 2026-10-27 - before the 11-12 decision - so index_deletions is empty on stale data, while the same regime record treats MSCI Standard deletions of BREN/TPIA/DSSA/CUAN as the defining regime evidence. The only name-level flow estimate in the source in this pack (Rp1.2tn for BRPT+BRMS combined, S17) is not quoted either, so the claim that the exit is absorbable is asserted without arithmetic. Required: refresh the registry entry with [S16], quote the flow estimate, and show the target and rating under the bear-regime compression.
challenges.answer: The flow event is now weight-bearing where it belongs: the combined Rp1.2tn BRPT/BRMS outflow estimate is a new fact (F56) quoted in the risks, F55 is cited in the summary, the bear-regime target is shown in sections 4 and 6 as the test of the other reading, and the 2026-10-27 registry snapshot is disclosed as stale. No DCF cash-flow change and no silent target cut; the registry edit is outside my scope and is flagged to the Director. [S16][S17][S0]

challenges.challenge: FY2026E np_parent (line) is about 2.5x the nine-month actual (F32) although Q4 revenue is only about a third of nine-month revenue - the forecast asks Q4 alone to earn more than the whole first nine months. Two causes are visible: interest_expense FY2026E is 12 percent on FY2025 closing debt while the nine-month accounts already show about US$20.4m of interest (S3 p.6 income statement), so Q4 interest comes out near US$2m; and the FY2025 unit cash cost (929.2/oz) is applied to the pushback-depressed 1H volumes that section 3 itself blames for the weak nine months. Required: reconcile FY2026E earnings to F31/F32 using the nine-month interest and a sourced 1H unit cost.
challenges.answer: FY2026E is now a bridge from the nine-month actual: revenue, COGS (F58) and interest (F57) sourced to S3 p.6; the FY2026E unit cash cost is set from the nine-month print (cost_per_bcm 590, other_cost_unit 500) and reverts to the FY2025 rate in FY2027E; cost_of_debt is raised to 14.3% so Q4 interest is charged rather than residual. [S3][S2]

challenges.challenge: Section 4 ranks underground timing beside the gold price as one of the three things that move value and says a two-year ramp delay is worth a similar amount to a 10 percent gold move, yet the only volume shock in the bear scenario is -10 percent (a.volume 0.9) and no timing or delay shock exists anywhere in the model. The risk the report itself calls primary is untested. Required: add a ramp-delay shock (or a delayed-plateau volume path) to the bear, or show the delay sensitivity and carry it into the scenario.
